description: Bump chart of seven pet types ranked by their estimated number of animals in each of four Animal Medicines Australia national surveys (2016, 2019, 2022 and 2025). Each line follows one pet type's rank from survey to survey.

text.signal: narrow ? ['Fish lead every survey;', 'cats have passed birds'] : 'Fish lead every survey; cats have passed birds'

subtitle.signal: narrow ? ['Pet types ranked by number of animals,', 'Australia, 2016 to 2025 · Rank 1 at the top'] : 'Pet types ranked by estimated number of animals, Australia, 2016 to 2025 · Rank 1 at the top'

signals.name: extraHeight
signals.description: Extra rank spacing set by the page so this card ends level with its paired card instead of leaving a gap.

signals.name: colorMuted
signals.description: Colour: the dark grey colour of small text: labels, axis words and notes. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-muted in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorHeading
signals.description: Colour: the dark blue colour of chart titles. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-heading in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorBorder
signals.description: Colour: light grey, used for gridlines, empty squares and places with no data. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-border in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorSurface
signals.description: Colour: white, the colour of the card each chart sits on. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-surface in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetDogs
signals.description: Colour: the colour for dogs (amber). This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-pet-dogs in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetCats
signals.description: Colour: the colour for cats (plum). This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-pet-cats in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetFish
signals.description: Colour: the colour for fish (teal). This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-pet-fish in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetBirds
signals.description: Colour: the colour for birds (green). This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-pet-birds in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetSmallMammals
signals.description: Colour: the colour for small mammals (violet). This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-pet-small-mammals in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetReptiles
signals.description: Colour: the colour for reptiles (raspberry). This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-pet-reptiles in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetOther
signals.description: Colour: the colour for other pets (grey). This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-pet-other in css/style.css.

signals.name: fontHeading
signals.description: Font: the fancy title font (DM Serif Display). This is only a backup; the real font comes from --font-heading in css/style.css.

signals.name: fontBody
signals.description: Font: the plain font for all other text (Fira Sans). This is only a backup; the real font comes from --font-body in css/style.css.

signals.name: width
signals.description: Measured by the loader; small-screen charts keep a compact minimum width.

signals.name: narrow
signals.description: Shorter labels and a three-line note for a compact chart; no data are removed.

signals.name: height
signals.description: Seven rank rows between the year labels and the note; rows spread out when the card is filled.

signals.name: leftX
signals.description: Where the first survey (2016) sits: leaves room for the pet names and counts on the left.

signals.name: rightX
signals.description: Where the last survey (2025) sits: leaves room for the pet names and counts on the right.

data.name: pets

transform.description: Put the surveys in time order so each line is drawn from 2016 to 2025.
Within each survey, rank the seven pet types by estimated number of animals (1 = most animals).
Keep the full pet type name beside the lines on every screen.

data.description: Each report's pet-type table, loaded unchanged; only the ranks and labels are derived.

data.name: firstSurvey
data.description: The 2016 rows, for the labels at the left end of each line.

data.name: lastSurvey
data.description: The 2025 rows, for the labels at the right end of each line.

data.name: years
data.description: The four survey years, written along the top.

marks.description: A faint vertical guide under each survey year.
The survey years along the top.
One line per pet type, joining its rank in each survey. Uniform stroke width avoids suggesting a quantity.

marks.name: rankPoints
marks.description: One dot per pet type per survey: its height shows that year's rank.
Left labels: each pet's name and its 2016 count, so colour is never the only cue.
Right labels: each pet's name and its 2025 count.
Reading note: ranks show order only, and close ranks are within survey error.

text.signal: narrow ? ['Ranked by estimated animals in each survey.', 'Labels give counts. Close ranks (5 to 7)', 'may swap within survey error.'] : ['Ranked by estimated number of animals in each survey; rank 1 is the largest.', 'Labels give counts. Close ranks, such as 5 to 7, may swap within survey error.']

usermeta.idiom: Bump chart: one category's rank tracked across successive time points (four surveys). Kirk, Table Idioms Part 2, bump chart.

scales.x: Survey year on a point scale; surveys are three years apart, so equal spacing is honest.
scales.rank: Ordinal rank mapped to equal vertical spacing; #1 is the most animals.

usermeta.codeGuide: Signals set the responsive layout and theme. Data transforms derive values; scales map them to positions and colours; marks draw the chart.
